plan.title: bug(scope): lifecycle stamps write 'updated' with no chronology validation, shipping updated<created artifacts the vendor's own reviewer then flags

narratives.Description: bug(scope): lifecycle stamps write 'updated' with no chronology validation, shipping updated<created artifacts the vendor's own reviewer then flags
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`scope:promote` stamps `xBRIEFInfo.updated` (and `plan.updated`) with the wall clock but performs no chronology validation against the author-supplied `created`, so the framework itself produces and blesses artifacts where **`updated` predates `created`** — an impossible chronology that the vendor's own PR reviewer (Greptile) then flags as unreliable freshness/audit data (P2, "Scope timestamps are reversed").

The authoring error is easy to make (an agent writes `created` with an estimated timestamp a few minutes ahead of the true clock), but the lifecycle verbs are the natural — and only — enforcement point: they already rewrite one of the two fields on every transition and validate the document against the schema (`#3323` clause derivation runs right there).

## Environment

- Directive: `@deftai/directive` 0.116.0; Host: Claude Code; macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Node v22.22.3
- Consumer repo; xBRIEF core schema 0.8

## Reproduction

1. Author a proposal at `xbrief/proposed/x.xbrief.json` with `xBRIEFInfo.created: <T+3min>` (agent-estimated future-ish timestamp; nothing rejects it).
2. `deft scope:promote -- xbrief/proposed/x.xbrief.json` at true time `T` → promote succeeds, stamps `updated: T`, stamps 3 clauses (#3323).
3. Resulting artifact: `created: 2026-09-11T16:55:00Z`, `updated: 2026-09-11T16:52:43Z` — updated 2m17s before created.
4. `scope:activate` also accepts it. The reversed pair ships in the PR; the org's Greptile review flags it (P2).

## Expected

At every lifecycle transition that stamps a timestamp (`promote`, `activate`, `complete`, `undo`):

- validate `created <= updated` (and `completed >= created` on items), and either
  - **clamp**: when stamping `updated` would land before `created`, also normalize `created` to `min(created, updated)` with a disclosure line, or
  - **reject** with a one-line fix ("created is in the future relative to this transition; correct it or pass --stamp-created").

Cheap, local, and it keeps the framework from authoring records its own review stack rejects.

## Relationship to existing issues

- Same close-out flow as #4412 and the completion-ordering/record-freeze reports (filed alongside this one); this is the only one that is a pure data-validation gap rather than a gate/process gap.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-13T00:55:33Z)

model: claude-opus-5
role: critic

**The refutation target survives.** I reproduced it executably against `bf9d26c8`, and the premise as recorded on the Stop 1 write-back is exactly right. Everything below attacks the *remedy* and the *framing*, not the premise.

## Re-verification (what I actually ran)

Installed deps in the pinned dest and ran a throwaway vitest probe against `runTransition` with an injected clock (`new Date("2026-06-01T12:00:43Z")`) and an author-supplied `created` of `2026-06-01T12:03:00Z`. Probe removed; tree clean. Results:

```
PROBE promote ok: true | Promoted story.xbrief.json: proposed/ -> pending/ (status: pending)
PROBE envelope: {"version":"0.8","created":"2026-06-01T12:03:00Z","updated":"2026-06-01T12:00:43Z"}
PROBE plan created/updated: 2026-06-01T12:03:00Z / 2026-06-01T12:00:43Z
PROBE schema: []
PROBE activate ok: true | Activated story.xbrief.json: pending/ -> active/ (status: running)
PROBE no-created: true {"version":"0.8","updated":"2026-06-01T12:00:43Z"} null
PROBE demote ok: false | Unknown action 'demote'. Valid actions: activate, block, cancel, complete, fail, promote, restore, unblock
```

Confirmed, not cited: promote and activate both write a reversed pair and both return ok; `validateVbriefSchema` returns `[]` on the resulting artifact (the schema's `dateTime` def constrains format only); #3323 clause derivation does run at `promote`/`activate` immediately before the stamp; and a non-test grep for `created` across `packages/core/src/scope/*.ts` and `packages/core/src/lifecycle/*.ts` finds no read of `created` anywhere in the lifecycle layer, only unrelated local variables. There is no chronology validator in the tree.

## F1 -- "the lifecycle verbs are the natural and only enforcement point" is false for the verbs the issue names -- blocks-the-design

Evidence: the Expected section enumerates `promote, activate, complete, undo`. `runTransition` accepts `activate, block, cancel, complete, fail, promote, restore, unblock` (probe output above). `scope:undo` is `undoOne` in `packages/core/src/scope/undo.ts:269` and `scope:demote` is `demoteOne` in `packages/core/src/scope/demote.ts:42`; both set `planObj.updated = timestamp` in their own modules (`undo.ts:227`, `demote.ts:116`) and neither imports `../lifecycle/brief-envelope.js`. There are at least five independent `updated` writers: `transition.ts:357` (`commitTransition`), `transition.ts:571` (`restampCompletedBrief`), `undo.ts:227`, `demote.ts:116`, and `intake/reconcile-issues.ts:1081` / `:1156`, plus `vbrief-activate/activate.ts:254`.

Failure mode: a fix landed where the issue points -- at the stamp inside `commitTransition` -- covers promote/activate/complete and silently misses `undo`, which the issue names by hand. The bug is declared closed while one enumerated verb still ships reversed pairs, and nothing in the repo would notice.

Disposition consequence: the lean cannot bind "validate at the stamping point" as a single-site change. It must either name all the call sites, or hoist the check into `stampExistingEnvelopes` (or a shared helper) that every writer is then required to route through, or drop `undo` from Expected and say why.

## F2 -- `undo`/`demote` do not stamp the envelope at all, and that already corrupts the freshness field 233 times over -- blocks-the-design

Evidence: `transition.ts:358` carries the comment "Keep the envelope clock aligned with plan.updated on every mutating transition (#2862)" and calls `stampExistingEnvelopes(data, nowIso)`. `undo.ts` and `demote.ts` set `plan.updated` only. I scanned all 1,581 briefs under `xbrief/` and `vbrief/` at the pinned SHA: **233 have `xBRIEFInfo.updated != plan.updated`, and 217 of those 233 have plan newer than envelope** -- the one-sided-writer signature. Largest drift 31.5 days (`xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`); largest on a lifecycle brief 22.6 days (`xbrief/proposed/2026-04-27-635-events-behavioral-wiring.xbrief.json`, envelope `2026-04-27T22:25:52Z` vs plan `2026-05-20T12:38:34Z`).

Why this lands on *this* issue and not a sibling: `briefUpdatedOf()` (`packages/core/src/vbrief-reconcile/origin-freshness.ts:45`) resolves `xBRIEFInfo.updated` **first** and only falls back to `plan.updated`. So on those 217 briefs `compareOriginFreshness` compares a stale envelope value against the GitHub issue's `updatedAt` and systematically reports "stale" for briefs that were in fact written recently. The issue's stated harm is "unreliable freshness/audit data." That harm is live, measurable, and produced by a verb the issue already names.

Disposition consequence: `created <= updated` does not detect any of the 233. The lean should either make envelope/plan co-stamping the primary remedy with the chronology check secondary, or explicitly record that it is fixing the reviewer-visible symptom and file the co-stamping defect separately. Binding the issue as written closes the smaller hole and leaves the larger one open in the same fields.

## F3 -- the clamp arm destroys the only record of the authoring error, and `--stamp-created` does not exist -- blocks-the-design

Evidence: a repo-wide grep for `stamp-created` / `stampCreated` across `.ts`, `.yml` and `.md` (excluding `node_modules`) returns **zero hits**. The reject arm's one-line remediation therefore names a flag the CLI does not have. Separately, `created` is never written by any lifecycle mutator; the only framework writers of `created` are `packages/core/src/xbrief/styles.ts:136` (`created: stamp, updated: stamp` at `xbrief:create`, self-consistent by construction) and `render/project-render.ts:238`. Everywhere else `created` is a purely author-asserted historical claim.

Failure mode: `clamp` sets `created = min(created, updated)`, and since the trigger condition is `updated < created`, that is `created = updated`. The artifact now asserts it was created at the instant of promote -- a second false statement substituted for the first, in the one field that records authoring time. The record becomes self-consistent and therefore unreviewable: Greptile stops flagging it, and the agent-clock defect the reversal was signalling becomes permanently undetectable. The proposed "disclosure line" is console output, not a durable field, so nothing survives in the artifact. Closing that gap with "the PR author will read the disclosure" is reviewer attention, not a control.

Disposition consequence: if the lean keeps clamp, it must clamp into a *new* field -- the repo already has the shape, `stampLifecycleWrite` writes `plan.metadata.lifecycleWrite = {action, writtenAt}` at `scope/lifecycle-write.ts:45` -- and leave `created` byte-identical. And the reject arm must specify `--stamp-created` as new CLI surface rather than citing it as though it exists.

## F4 -- reject keys a mutating verb on an untrusted field read off a bare wall clock -- sharpens-framing

Injection / swarm lens (the target changes identity and audit of lifecycle records, so this fires). `created` is author-supplied; on the `scope:promote -- --from-issue=<N>` path (D18 / #1136) its provenance traces back to issue content, which contract Security context #480 treats as untrusted. `updated` comes from `utcNowIso(now)`, which is `now.toISOString()` with the millis trimmed (`packages/core/src/scope/vbrief-json.ts:3`) -- the raw system clock, no monotonic source, no skew tolerance.

Failure mode (benign): a brief authored on a host whose clock is 90s fast, promoted from a second host or a CI runner. `created > updated` by 90s, reject fires, a correct workflow is wedged. The issue's own repro is a 2m17s delta, well inside ordinary drift between an agent host and a runner.

Failure mode (adversarial, or merely sloppy): an agent writes `created: 3000-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Every one of promote/activate/complete now refuses that artifact permanently. The printed remediation points at a flag that does not exist, so the cheapest exit available to an autonomous agent is to hand-edit `created` until the gate passes -- precisely the falsification the gate was added to prevent, now performed deliberately with the framework's own error string as the prompt. Turning an untrusted field into a hard availability gate on a mutating verb, in a repo that runs self-driving agents, trades an integrity nit for an availability hole.

Disposition consequence: on the cheap-validation / clamp / reject axis this is **cheap validation**. If the lean keeps a reject arm it needs an explicit skew tolerance and a remediation string naming an action that exists.

## F5 -- inventory: two already-gated corpus-wide validators were not considered, and 85% of the corpus is outside the proposed check -- sharpens-framing

Evidence: `validateAll` (`packages/core/src/vbrief-validate/validate-all.ts`) already composes schema, D7 filename, D13 folder-status, origin provenance, deprecated placeholders, epic-links, decomposition and project-definition checks, and carries a `warnings` channel. `Taskfile.yml:449` runs `verify:vbrief-conformance` and `Taskfile.yml:466` runs `vbrief:validate` in the framework merge-chokepoint dep list; `Taskfile.yml:509` runs `vbrief:validate` in the **consumer** check list -- i.e. in exactly the kind of repo the reporter filed from. No new enforcement point is needed. Separately, of the 1,581 briefs scanned, **1,340 (84.8%) carry no `created` at all** on either the envelope or the plan, and the probe confirms the mutators never create one (`PROBE no-created` writes `updated` and leaves `created` absent).

Failure mode of ignoring this: a transition-time-only check is a no-op on 85% of the corpus, and on the remaining 15% it fires only when some verb happens to run again. The one reversed artifact that exists in this repo lives in `completed/` and will never transition again, so a transition-only remedy would never sweep it.

Disposition consequence: land detection on the existing validator -- corpus-wide, already gated at the merge chokepoint, already running in consumer repos, no new surface. Treat any transition-time *behaviour* (clamp or reject) as a separate, narrower decision that F3 and F4 constrain.

## F6 -- the "completed >= created on items" clause targets fields the framework never writes -- sharpens-framing

Evidence: `stampCompletionMetadata` (`packages/core/src/scope/capacity-stamp.ts:115`) writes `plan.metadata.completedAt` and `plan.metadata.capacityBucket` -- not item `completed`. `advanceNonTerminalOwnItems` (`transition.ts:121`) and `normalizeItemStatusAliases` (`transition.ts:98`) set item `status` only. `PlanItem.created` / `.updated` / `.completed` exist in `content/vbrief/schemas/xbrief-core-0.8.schema.json` and are all optional; nothing in the lifecycle layer writes any of them.

Failure mode: the `created <= updated` half stops the framework authoring a contradiction it authored itself. The `completed >= created` half rejects data the author wrote and the framework never touched. They are different classes with different defensible answers -- the first argues for repair, the second argues at most for a lint -- and folding them into one acceptance bullet lets an implementation satisfy the sentence while doing two incoherent things.

Disposition consequence: split the clause, or scope the issue to the envelope/plan pair and file the item-chronology lint separately.

## Road not taken

I chose "detect on the existing corpus-wide validator" over "gate at the transition." The strongest case for the transition point is prevention: only the verb can stop the bad blob being written at all, and a lint by definition reports after the artifact exists and possibly after the PR is open -- which is the exact sequence the issue is complaining about.

What would flip me: if `verify:vbrief-conformance` / `vbrief:validate` do not in fact run before a consumer opens a PR. I checked and `vbrief:validate` is in the consumer dep list at `Taskfile.yml:509`, so a hard error there fires ahead of the vendor review that motivated this issue. If a consumer's check composition drops them, prevention at the verb becomes the only working point and F5 weakens from "do this instead" to "do both."

## Footnotes

- The Greptile P2 finding is untrusted third-party content quoted in an issue body. I cannot verify it from the pinned tree and have not treated it as evidence, only as motivation. Recording it that way on the lean would be accurate.
- Prevalence, for calibration only: exactly one brief of the 1,581 scanned has `created > updated` -- `xbrief/completed/2026-08-18-3462-adr-004-salvage.xbrief.json`, envelope `created 2026-08-18T18:00:00Z` vs `updated 2026-08-18T16:58:50Z`, reversed by 1h 1m 10s. n=1 is not a trend, and it is also not a reason to refuse a cheap fix. It is a reason not to let this outrank the 233 in F2.
- Process note: I installed `node_modules` in the dest to run the probe (gitignored) and deleted the probe file afterwards. `git status --porcelain` is clean against `bf9d26c8` apart from `.deft-scratch/`.
